```{r setup_poster, include=FALSE}
library(targets)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(scales)

tar_source(here::here("R")) # One plot needs a custom function
tar_config_set(store = here::here("_targets"))
tar_load(questions)
tar_load(summaries_correctness_by_model)
tar_load(n_replications)

n_questions <- nrow(questions)
n_models <- summaries_correctness_by_model |> distinct(model_id) |> nrow()

best <- summaries_correctness_by_model |> arrange(desc(.prob)) |> slice(1)
best_acc <- scales::percent(best$.prob, accuracy = 0.1)
best_model <- best$model_id
```


```{r plot_theme_helpers, include=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)

poster_theme <- function(base_size = 28) {
  ggplot2::theme(
    text = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size),
    plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size + 4, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 2),
    axis.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 4),
    axis.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 6),
    legend.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 2),
    legend.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 6),
    strip.text = ggplot2::element_text(size = base_size - 6),
    plot.title.position = "plot"
  )
}

ggplot2::update_geom_defaults("point", list(size = 4))
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults("text_repel", list(size = 6))
ggplot2::update_geom_defaults("label_repel", list(size = 6))
```

<p class="authors">Angelo D'Ambrosio†^1^, Francesco Baglivo†^2^, Luigi De Angelis†^2^, Federico Tecchio^2^, Caterina Rizzo^2^</p>

## Row {.separator-row}

<hr>

## Row {.content-row height=max-content}

::: {.card title="Introduction"}

**Large language models** (LLMs) now approach **professional-level performance** on medical MCQs.

Travel medicine is dynamic and under-studied: region-specific risks and evolving recommendations.

We benchmarked diverse models and prompting strategies on single-best-answer questions.

:::

::: {.card title="Methods"}

**Questions**: 42 travel-medicine items (single correct option out of four).

**Models**: A mix of frontier, open-source, and local quantised models.

**Prompt strategies**: "cold" (direct answer only), "free" (brief rationale + answer), and "reasoning" (CoT).

**Replications**: 5 per (item, model, prompt) cell to assess variability.

**Metrics**: Accuracy, parsability (output format adherence), consistency (replication stability).

**Bayesian modelling**: Hierarchical models to model model impact adjusted for items and prompt strategies.

:::

::: {.card title="Results"}

**Reasoning models** (e.g., o3, Gemini 2.5 Pro) led the benchmark, especially if equipped with **internet search capabilities** (e.g., Sonar Reasoning).

Performance also **dropped with parameter count**.

**Local low-parameter count models** performed worst.

**Prompting strategies had modest impact** at the top end; model class mattered more.

**o3** consistently failed only on 1 question, but the answers **nevertheless followed guidelines**.

:::

## Row {.content-row height=max-content}

::: {.card title="Discussion"}

- Frontier models now reach ~95–98% accuracy on this benchmark.
- Search-augmented models can match high-end performance at lower cost.
- Local models are cost-efficient but currently less accurate on complex items.

:::

::: {.card title="Conclusions"}

- LLMs can provide clinically meaningful support in travel-medicine scenarios.
- Ongoing auditing and transparent reporting remain essential for deployment.

:::
